US federal employees to work in Taiwan government offices under scheme to strengthen ties
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The main objectives of the programme are to expand and strengthen the US-Taiwan partnership, as well as US officials’ expertise regarding Taiwan.
Published Nov 11, 2026, 01:58 PM
Updated Nov 11, 2026, 03:30 PM
US federal employees will work in Taiwan offices for up to one year under a new Taiwan Fellowship Programme to deepen ties and build Mandarin skills.
The AIT said the scheme will place fellows in parliamentary offices, ministries and other bodies, and aims to expand the US-Taiwan partnership.
The plan shows strong bipartisan support, but it may upset China, which sees Taiwan as its most sensitive issue and opposes closer US contacts.
TAIPEI – Some US federal employees will work in Taiwan government offices for up to one year under a new scheme to strengthen already close ties between Taipei and Washington, the de facto US embassy said on Nov 11.
The United States, like most countries, has no formal diplomatic ties with Chinese-claimed Taiwan, but is its most important international backer and arms supplier – a persistent sticking point in its relations with Beijing.
Under the new Taiwan Fellowship Programme (TFP), which is funded under Washington’s 2023 Taiwan Fellowship Act, US federal employees will spend up to one year in intensive Mandarin language training and studies.
“Upon completion of training, the Fellows are expected to work, for up to one year, in Taiwan parliamentary offices, ministries, other agencies or offices, or organisations outside the public sector in Taiwan,” the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) said in a statement.
The main objectives of the programme are to expand and strengthen the US-Taiwan partnership, as well as US officials’ expertise regarding Taiwan, it added, without saying how many people would take part each year.
The programme will build a group of federal professionals with language skills, cultural knowledge and “lasting working relationships across Taiwan”.
The memorandum of understanding for the programme was signed on Nov 10 in the United States, it added.
“TFP reflects strong bipartisan support for the US-Taiwan relationship and a shared commitment to the people-to-people ties at its core,” AIT managing director Ingrid Larson said in the statement.
In 1994, the US Congress established a similar scheme for Japan, called the Mike Mansfield Fellowship.
AIT’s large, fortress-like office in Taipei functions like an embassy.
China says Taiwan is its most important and sensitive diplomatic issue and has repeatedly demanded Washington curtail its contacts with Taipei and end arms sales.
US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet next week for the third time this year on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders summit in Shenzhen. REUTERS

台湾当局证实，黄丽娟持香港护照进入台湾，她的许可证已被吊销。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 11 日 1:32
更新于 2026 年 11 月 11 日 1:47
台湾称爱丽丝黄持香港护照入境，官员正在调查她在与英伟达老板黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的指控。
Nvidia 于 11 月 8 日对黄仁勋展开调查，而北京否认了间谍指控，台湾表示正在检查安全程序。
台湾内政部长表示，黄现在在海外，她的许可证被吊销，她不能再入境；此案引发了国家安全担忧。
台北——台湾移民机构 11 月 11 日表示，在当局调查这一事件时，被指控在与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染期间为中国从事间谍活动的女子使用香港护照进入台湾。
据报道，黄仁勋承认与新加坡Megaspeed公司前中国高管爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，美国官员认为她为中国情报机构工作。北京否认了间谍指控。
Nvidia 董事会于 11 月 8 日宣布，已对该公司首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 展开调查，黄仁勋与 Alice Huang 没有关系。
入出国及移民署署长林弘恩对记者表示，“我国政府相关部门已充分了解相关记录和信息”，并证实黄丽娟曾使用香港护照进入台湾。
“我们知道她所有的相关出入境记录。”
一般来说，香港护照持有者比持有中国大陆护照的人更容易进入台湾，后者还必须申请特别许可才能前往台湾。
额外的限制部分是由于中国与台湾之间的复杂关系，北京声称并誓言要将台湾置于其控制之下。
台湾内政部长刘世芳表示，黄丽娟“确实入境了，但目前在海外”。
“如果我们知道她是间谍，我们肯定不会让她进入台湾，”刘告诉国会议员。
她说：“我们将审查我们的程序，特别是预筛选、临时抽查和访谈以及访问后措施。”
“据我们了解，这名黄女士的通行证已被吊销，这意味着她不可能再次进入台湾。”
11月10日，刘表示台湾“国安部门正在积极调查此事”。
2025 年 5 月，台湾顶级科技博览会台北国际电脑展期间，黄仁勋 (Alice Huang)，又名黄乐 (Huang Le)，出席了黄仁勋在台北一家中餐厅举办的晚宴。
记者站在餐厅外，透过玻璃门窗拍摄黄仁勋和一名身穿粉色连衣裙、名叫爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 的女子与其他与会者混在一起的情况。
据现场直播显示，有一次，黄仁勋用手臂搂住黄爱丽丝，她亲吻了他的右脸颊。法新社

Jensen Huang probe: Chinese woman entered Taiwan on HK passport | The Straits Times
Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia boss Jensen Huang entered Taiwan on Hong Kong passport
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Taiwanese authorities confirmed that Alice Huang had entered Taiwan on a Hong Kong passport, and that her permit has since been revoked.
Published Nov 11, 2026, 01:32 PM
Updated Nov 11, 2026, 01:47 PM
Taiwan said Alice Huang entered on a Hong Kong passport, as officials investigate claims she spied for China during an affair with Nvidia boss Jensen Huang.
Nvidia opened a probe into Jensen Huang on Nov 8, while Beijing denied the spying claims and Taiwan said it is checking security procedures.
Taiwan’s Interior Minister said Huang is now overseas, her permit was revoked, and she cannot enter again; the case has raised national security concerns.
TAIPEI – The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang had used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan, the island’s immigration agency said on Nov 11, as the authorities investigate the incident.
Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a Chinese former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the spying allegations.
Nvidia’s board announced on Nov 8 that it had opened a probe into Jensen Huang, the company’s chief executive and co-founder, who is no relation to Alice Huang.
“Our government’s relevant agencies are fully informed of the relevant records and information,” National Immigration Agency Director-General Lin Horng-en told reporters, confirming that Alice Huang had used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan.
“We were aware of all her relevant entry and exit records.”
It is generally easier for Hong Kong passport holders to enter Taiwan than those with mainland Chinese passports, who must also apply for special permission to travel there.
The additional restrictions are partly due to the complex relations between China and Taiwan, which Beijing claims and has vowed to bring under its control.
Taiwan’s Interior Minister Liu Shyh-fang said Alice Huang “did indeed enter the country, but she is currently overseas”.
“If we had known she was a spy, we certainly would not have let her enter Taiwan,” Liu told lawmakers in Parliament.
“We will review our procedures, specifically our pre-screening, interim spot checks and interviews, and post-visit measures,” she said.
“As far as we understand, this Ms Huang has had her permit revoked, meaning it is impossible for her to enter Taiwan again.”
On Nov 10, Liu said Taiwan’s “national security units are actively investigating the matter”.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was seen at a dinner in May 2025 hosted by Jensen Huang at a Chinese restaurant in Taipei during Computex, the island’s top tech expo.
Journalists stood outside the restaurant filming through glass windows and doors as Jensen Huang and a woman identified as Alice Huang, who was wearing a pink dress, mingled with other attendees.
At one point, Jensen Huang can be seen putting his arm around Alice Huang as she kisses him on the right cheek, press live streams show. AFP

title: (FRA獨家）特習會前北京醞釀五項貿易要求 涉關稅芯片及投資
summary: 特朗普與習近平計劃在APEC高峰會上進行今年第三次會唔。消息人士指出，中方醞釀提出五項貿易訴求，包括關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制等。 (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP) 美國中期選舉之後，亞太經合組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議將於本月18日至19日在深圳舉行，美國總統特朗普預計與中國國家主席習近平在會議期間舉行今年第三次會面。 北京一位外貿部門人士向本臺透露，中方醞釀的五項貿易訴求涉及關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制、中國企業赴美投
content: 特朗普與習近平計劃在APEC高峰會上進行今年第三次會唔。消息人士指出，中方醞釀提出五項貿易訴求，包括關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制等。 (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP) 美國中期選舉之後，亞太經合組織（APEC）領導人非正式會議將於本月18日至19日在深圳舉行，美國總統特朗普預計與中國國家主席習近平在會議期間舉行今年第三次會面。 北京一位外貿部門人士向本臺透露，中方醞釀的五項貿易訴求涉及關稅、農產品採購、先進芯片及設備出口限制、中國企業赴美投資，以及跨境合規與多邊規則。其中，中方要求美方取消全部對華加徵關稅，落實農產品貿易便利化及關稅減讓安排，放寬先進芯片出口限制，併為中國企業赴美投資提供非歧視的營商環境。 北京擬要求取消對華加徵關稅 另一位不願公開身份和職務的人士說：“中方將要求美方徹底取消全部對華加徵關稅，還會提出以市場化原則積極擴大自美農產品進口，但前提是美方必須營造相應的貿易便利化條件，並切實給予關稅減讓。” 他還表示：“中方還要求美方停止對中國科技企業的無理打壓，停止將經貿科技問題泛安全化，並放寬相關先進芯片及設備的出口限制。” 上週四（5日），中國商務部發言人黃玲表示，中方對擴大采購美國農產品持開放態度，但前提是雙方達成的各涉及300億美元商品的對等降稅安排落實。她希望美方與中方共同降低關稅、減少非關稅壁壘及擴大市場準入。路透社報道，這項涉及雙方合計600億美元商品的降稅安排尚未最終落實。 中國外交部本週六發佈的消息顯示，中美經貿中方牽頭人、國務院副總理何立峰於本週五（6日）晚與美國財政部長貝森特、貿易代表格里爾舉行視頻通話，討論落實兩國元首北京和華盛頓會晤共識及經貿磋商成果。 另一位接近中國商務部的人士稱，中方正在考慮要求美方為中國電動車、電池及能源設備等企業赴美投資提供非歧視的營商環境。相關要求涉及中國企業在美國的市場準入、投資審查及經營條件。 習近平於2026年9月23日至25日對美國進行國事訪問期間，與特朗普就經貿問題達成多項共識，包括對雙方各約300億美元非敏感商品給予更優惠的關稅待遇，以及推進雙邊貿易和投資磋商機制。雙方還將此前達成的貿易休戰安排延長至2027年1月。相關關稅減讓措施尚未最終落實。 學者：中期選舉改變中美談判氣氛 研究中美關係的學者姚賦（化名）接受採訪時表示，在美國中期選舉改變美國政治格局之後，深圳APEC峰會期間的中美會晤氣氛也發生變化：“面對受到國會制約的特朗普，習肯定將利用特朗普剩下兩年執政，最大化習或中國的利益，包括貿易戰和臺灣問題等，並且以既定的所謂三巨頭峰會滿足特的虛榮心，製造其權力幻想。相信，習會趁機要求特在關稅、芯片等經貿問題上讓步，取消高關稅。” 姚賦進一步表示：“不過，是否達成合作成果仍然決定於特朗普本人能否說服習暫停對伊朗援助。畢竟關稅問題相比美伊戰爭，後者對特更為重要。目前局勢既有利於中方，看起來，習只要稍微在伊朗問題做出輕微讓步，便可從特朗普處大幅改善中美貿易關係和談判。” 資深評論人士蔡慎坤對本臺表示，美國中期選舉後，特朗普受到國會制約，北京可能調整對美談判策略。他說：“川普有可能不再堅持過去那麼強硬的貿易政策。因為他知道如果再堅持，中方會繼續的拖延，去年他們在釜山達成的協議現在已經不了了之，中國實際上一直在觀察，也在等待美國中期選舉。因為中期選舉川普輸了之後，很多制衡政策使得他很難發力了。” 談及臺灣問題，蔡慎坤錶示，北京希望特朗普在反對臺獨問題上作出表態，但美國兩黨在臺灣問題上的立場接近，特朗普讓步的空間有限。他認為，北京近期對臺灣採取軍事行動的可能性不大，2028年之後的政治變化可能影響臺海局勢。 對於中美俄三國領導人是否在深圳舉行會談，北京一位知情人士表示，中方目前對烏克蘭問題關注有限，更重視解決中美貿易摩擦及美國對臺軍售問題。他說：“今天已經8號了，還沒聽說特朗普、普京和習近平舉行三國元首會談已進入議事日程。” 伊朗問題成會談進展風向標 伊朗問題也是判斷中美高層會談能否取得進展的其中一個風向標。姚賦分析稱，北京在伊朗問題上的立場可能影響特朗普對華貿易談判的考慮。

content:
由美日印澳“四方安全对话”成员国派遣多艘军舰参与的“马拉巴尔 2026”海上军事演习目前持续在日本关东地区以南海域进行，演习的重点在于强化印太区域内的反潜及反水面作战。美国第七舰队表示，此次演习旨在支持“自由开放的印太地区”，并强化各方共同维护地区稳定、安全与繁荣，以及威慑侵略者的决心。
“马拉巴尔 2026”海上军事演习的主办单位日本海上自卫队9日在官方X平台上贴出短片，并附上贴文表示，“通过此次由海上自卫队主办的演习，我们将进一步加强与各参演国之间的合作，共同致力于实现“自由开放的印度太平洋”。
“马拉巴尔 2026”演习于11月5日开始持续到12日，在横须贺海军基地周边海域及岸上展开演练。
本次演习中，美国派出两栖船坞运输舰“安克雷奇”号 (USS Anchorage, LPD-23)和“约翰·P·穆尔萨”号，以及P-8A“海神”反潜巡逻机。
日本海上自卫队派出直升机驱逐舰“伊势”号 (JS Ise)、护卫舰“最上”号 (JS Mogami)、一艘苍龙级潜艇以及 P-1 反潜巡逻机。
印度派出东部舰队的国产导弹隐身护卫舰“萨亚德里号” (INS Sahyadri)。
澳大利亚派出护卫舰“斯图尔特”号 (HMAS Stuart)和 P-8A“海神”反潜巡逻机。
演练科目涵盖反潜战 (ASW)、反水面战 (ASUW)、防空与网络防御、以及多国海上联合协调行动等全方位多领域训练。
今年是“马拉巴尔”演习的30周年，也是美日印澳四国第6次共同参与“马拉巴尔”演习。
美国第七舰队司令帕特·汉尼芬（Pat Hannifin）中将表示，“‘马拉巴尔’演习始于1992年，最初只是美印之间一项规模较小的双边活动；经过30年的发展，现已演变为一场顶级的四边演习。这种发展提升了我们的互操作性，使我们能够携手巩固一个造福各国的‘自由开放的印太地区’。”
10月底在美国亚特兰大举行的“四方安全对话”外长会议中也决定，基于今年5月达成的“印太海上监视协作倡议”框架，四国将在2027年举行第一次“海龙2027”（Sea Dragon 2027）演习，以加强信息共享和海域态势感知。

title: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
summary: PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery | TechCrunch PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery 11:03 AM PST · November 10, 2026 David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member
content:
PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery | TechCrunch
PSI is trying to make a business out of AI-driven scientific discovery
11:03 AM PST · November 10, 2026
David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI), used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an 18-year-old problem about quantum computing.
“I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?”
The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.
The solution appears to close the door on one avenue quantum computers could follow to solve certain difficult problems at high speed, but not all of them. “It’s a negative result that allows people to know, okay, we’re no longer looking there,” Turturean said.
More broadly, it reflects the upheaval in the scientific world caused by AI problem-solving.
“A proof of full [Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture] was one of the last remaining open problems in quantum query complexity that everyone seemed to agree was centrally important,” Aaronson, who described himself feeling satisfied, awestruck, disappointed, and fatigued by the news, wrote. “I was surprised, honestly, to see it missing from OpenAI’s Mathocalypse dump a few weeks ago. Surely they tried it, so was it really so much harder than all the problems that were solved?”
That’s a point in favor of PSI’s model, which is to solve scientific problems with specialized model harnesses and scaffolding.
“An effective kind of research system should have lots of things related to harnesses, lots related to tools, memory systems, simulation infrastructure,” PSI CEO Matt Pines told TechCrunch. “You want to be able to really go after a problem at breadth and depth, and be able to consider a wide range of potential alternatives.”
For now, the company’s revenue comes from using its tools to optimize data centers, simulating the variables of heat, power, water, sound — “where the performance of that site as well as its impact on the community are a direct function of its physics.” The long play, however, is converting theoretical physics breakthroughs into actual technologies.
“Six to nine months ago, when I was talking to investors, like I had to sort of stretch to validate that conditional, right? Like, ‘no, no, no, trust me, pretty soon, theoretical physics is going to be mostly the domain of machines,’” Pines said. “And it’s not there yet, but it’s on its way.”
Still, while AI has claimed important solutions in fields like mathematics and computer science where it’s possible to express them in validated code, doing so in less abstracted disciplines like the life sciences or physics has proven more difficult. Last week, the startup Discovered Materials released a $1 million grand challenge for researchers using AI to understand problems like superconductivity and heat dissipation.
“At the end of the day, physics is different than math because it’s the real world … nature gets a vote in your models of reality,” Pines said. He said the startup is focused on understanding how to take computational results and validate them with experiments in the most efficient way possible.
“If it’s a true fact of nature, that’s a trick that you can exploit,” Pines said. “You could build a device out of it, right? The AI suggests an idea; it allows you to do something in the world you weren’t able to do before … and so each of those are kind of loops that PSI is building.”
As “neolabs for science” become a pathway for potentially groundbreaking science, the participants are still figuring out what the standards are for this new world. Because PSI had to hold its result until Anthropic’s model was nearly ready for release, they were able to share it with relevant researchers to better understand it.
“As an academic, we wanted to play our role in doing things the right way,” Jim Halverson, a professor at Northeastern University who advises PSI, said. He’ll be attending a summit at MIT next week where leading physicists will try to hash out a response to the new pace of science. “Best practices are still emerging … We figured that transparency is a good way to go, and contacting experts is a good way to go.”
“We had some time to sit on it … and it was the first time that I actually took one of my AI-elicited solutions on print, and I read through it, and I was like, okay, how can I make this … be presented more naturally for a human?” Turturean, who said the academic community will expect him to be able to explain the result, told TechCrunch. “And I think it also made me realize, oh my God, the weight of what AI can do.”

记录显示，与解放军有联系的中国大学尽管被美国列入黑名单，仍购买了 Nvidia H200 芯片海峡时报
记录显示，与解放军有联系的中国大学尽管被美国列入黑名单，仍购买了 Nvidia H200 芯片
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
发表于 2026 年 11 月 11 日 1:33
更新于 2026 年 11 月 11 日 03:49
北京，11 月 11 日 - 采购记录显示，一所与中国人民解放军关系密切的中国大学上个月购买了英伟达强大的 H200 人工智能芯片，尽管该芯片被列入美国出口黑名单，这突显了华盛顿在遏制中国获取先进技术方面的差距。
这些调查结果发布之际，英伟达及其首席执行官黄仁勋在华盛顿面临着越来越严格的审查，因为他游说放宽对中国销售人工智能芯片的限制，有报道称他成为中国间谍活动的目标。
黄认为，美国继续向中国销售将保持美国的技术领先地位，并使中国客户继续依赖美国技术。但一些美国立法者表示，使用英伟达最强大的人工智能芯片可以加速中国用于武器设计、情报分析和军事现代化的人工智能系统的开发。
国会中的民主党人和共和党人都敦促对中国获得先进人工智能芯片进行更严格的控制，例如芯片跟踪要求和加强国会对出口的监督。三名共和党国会委员会主席已要求于 11 月 18 日就黄与一名涉嫌中国情报人员接触的报道向黄进行通报。
西北工业大学是中国“国防七子”精英国防大学成员之一，根据其网站上 10 月 21 日的采购记录，上个月以 874,700 元（123,000 美元）的价格购买了两块 H200 芯片。
记录显示，该管理学院的芯片是从陕西博算网络科技有限公司购买的，而不是直接从英伟达购买的。
H200 是英伟达最强大的用于训练和运行先进人工智能系统的芯片之一，并且需要获得美国出口许可证的批准，而西北工业大学等列入黑名单的机构通常会被拒绝获得出口许可证。
采购记录显示，西北工业大学今年还通过五份向中国公司租用计算能力的合同，购买了 H200 芯片和其他强大的 Nvidia AI 处理器。
路透社首次报道了芯片采购和计算合同。西北工业大学、英伟达和负责监督出口管制的美国商务部工业与安全局没有回应置评请求。路透社无法确定陕西博算网络科技的联系方式。
西北工业学院位于西北城市西安，从事军用飞机、导弹和卫星相关的研究。
2001 年，美国商务部因该大学涉嫌参与导弹扩散活动和军事研究而将其列入贸易黑名单（即“实体名单”）。它在 2019 年收紧了限制，在大多数情况下，向该大学出口受管制的美国技术的许可都受到拒绝政策的约束。
西北工业大学的采购表明，与军事有联系的中国机构如何继续通过国内供应商获得美国人工智能计算能力，要么直接购买芯片，要么租用包含芯片的服务器。

PLA-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist, records show | The Straits Times
PLA-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist, records show
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Published Nov 11, 2026, 01:33 PM
Updated Nov 11, 2026, 03:49 PM
BEIJING, Nov 11 - A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology.
The findings come as Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang face mounting scrutiny in Washington over his lobbying for looser restrictions on sales of AI chips to China, following reports alleging he was targeted by a Chinese spying operation.
Huang has argued that continued US sales to China would preserve American technological leadership and keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology. But some US lawmakers say access to Nvidia's most powerful AI chips can speed China's development of AI systems for weapons design, intelligence analysis and military modernisation.
Both Democrats and Republicans in Congress have urged stronger controls on China's access to advanced AI chips, such as chip-tracking requirements and greater congressional oversight of exports. Three Republican congressional committee chairmen have requested a briefing with Huang on November 18 over his reported contacts with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative.
Northwestern Polytechnical University, a member of China's "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of elite defence-focused universities, bought two H200 chips last month for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), according to an October 21 procurement record on its website.
The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows.
The H200 is among Nvidia's most capable chips for training and running advanced AI systems and is subject to US export licence approvals, which are normally denied for blacklisted institutions such as Northwestern Polytechnical.
Northwestern Polytechnical also bought access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia AI processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies, procurement records show.
Reuters is reporting the chip purchases and computing contracts for the first time. Northwestern Polytechnical, Nvidia and the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export controls, did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not determine contact details for Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology.
Based in the northwestern city of Xian, Northwestern Polytechnical conducts research related to military aircraft, missiles and satellites.
The US Commerce Department added the university to its trade blacklist, known as the Entity List, in 2001 over its alleged involvement in missile-proliferation activities and military research. It tightened the restrictions in 2019, making licences for exports of controlled US technology to the university subject to a policy of denial in most circumstances.
Northwestern Polytechnical's purchases show how Chinese institutions with military ties continue to obtain US AI computing power through domestic suppliers, either by buying chips outright or renting access to servers containing them.
A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers. Several had close links to China's defence industry or military research.
The universities named in the records did not respond to requests for comment.
NVIDIA CHIPS FOR MILITARY-LINKED RESEARCH
US President Donald Trump's administration began allowing some H200 exports to China on a case-by-case basis in January. But that policy did not lift the separate restrictions applying to Entity List organisations such as Northwestern Polytechnical.
The January licensing rules also require safeguards to prevent blacklisted entities and military end-users from remotely accessing chips exported under the policy, which covers H200 processors and less advanced models.
In addition to the management school's outright purchase of the two H200 chips, procurement records show the university's cybersecurity school awarded two seven-month contracts in January for access to servers containing eight H200 chips each. The contracts, worth 441,700 yuan and 441,000 yuan, covered fine-tuning AI models and reinforcement-learning training.
It also rented access to servers containing eight Nvidia A100 chips and eight A800 chips. The A100 and A800 are banned from export to all Chinese entities, though the H200 is the most advanced of those cited in Northwestern Polytechnical's procurement records.
In April, another university institute bought computing services requiring at least 24 A100 chips in a 375,000 yuan contract for structural and fluid-dynamics simulations.
The awards went to several little-known Chinese technology suppliers. The records offered scant information about where the processors originated or where the rented servers operated.
Under Chinese law, public procurement agencies must verify that suppliers can fulfil orders before announcing winning bidders and signing contracts.
The procurement records show a wider market for restricted Nvidia AI chips and computing services at Chinese universities.
Shenzhen University bought three H100 processors, another high-end Nvidia AI chip banned by the US, for 769,800 yuan in September. Wuhan University of Technology bought a server containing an H100 chip for 355,000 yuan in June and four A100 chips in a separate 344,000 yuan purchase, the records show.
Beihang University, another of the Seven Sons of National Defense universities, bought four A800 processors for 489,000 yuan in April. Beihang has close ties to China's aerospace and defence industries and conducts research for military aviation and space programmes.
Two government procurement announcements in July and September named suppliers selected to provide computing services using Nvidia H800 and A800 chips restricted from export to China to the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. One listed H800 access at 10 yuan per chip-hour. A separate January procurement award named a supplier of six A100 chips worth 484,800 yuan for a Shenzhen-based public institution.
Reuters has previously reported that Chinese institutions acquired restricted Nvidia chips embedded in servers made by Super Micro Computer, Dell and Gigabyte through domestic resellers. Reuters has also documented an underground market in China for restricted Nvidia chips sourced from overseas inventories and third-country intermediaries.
Last week, Reuters reported that small quantities of H200 chips had reached China through indirect routes while Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports. REUTERS

11月10日，香港演员梁家辉凭借《影锋》在厦门举行的第39届金鸡奖颁奖典礼上首次获得金鸡奖最佳男主角奖。他形容这场胜利是“神奇的”，并感谢导演杨致远、成龙和特技团队。
香港资深演员梁家辉凭借与成龙联袂主演的《影锋》，首次获得第39届金鸡奖最佳男主角奖。颁奖典礼于11月10日在厦门举行，由郭富城、朱一龙颁奖。
从事电影行业40多年的梁振英表示，这是他第一次获得金鸡奖提名并获奖，并将这段经历描述为“神奇”和“梦幻般”。他在获奖感言中感谢导演杨伟利、成龙和成龙特技团队，并补充说这个奖项提醒他继续磨练演技。

title: How China gets the Nvidia chips it needs to develop AI
zh_title: 中国如何获得开发人工智能所需的英伟达芯片
summary: 据报道，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一家新加坡公司的一名中国高管有染，美国怀疑该公司向中国走私人工智能微芯片。 Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。照片：英伟达。该丑闻将人们的注意力集中在中国这个人工智能大国如何在美国的出口限制下获得尖端芯片。为什么 Nvidia 芯片如此重要？ Nvidia 设计的先进组件最初是为了处理视频游戏中的 3D 视觉效果而设计的，称为图形处理单元 (GPU)。这些有能力粉碎巨大的情绪
content:
据报道，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一家新加坡公司的一名中国高管有染，美国怀疑该公司向中国走私人工智能微芯片。 Nvidia 的 H200 芯片。照片：英伟达。该丑闻将人们的注意力集中在中国这个人工智能大国如何在美国的出口限制下获得尖端芯片。为什么 Nvidia 芯片如此重要？ Nvidia 设计的先进组件最初是为了处理视频游戏中的 3D 视觉效果而设计的，称为图形处理单元 (GPU)。它们能够处理大量数字数据，因此也可大规模用于训练和运行人工智能。 ChatGPT 于 2022 年推出，展示了人工智能的潜力，随着政府和科技巨头竞相进一步开发该技术，引发了投资淘金热。 Nvidia 总部位于加利福尼亚州圣克拉拉。照片：英伟达。随着芯片订单的涌入，英伟达的市值已飙升至 4.5 万亿美元，目前与苹果并列全球市值最高的两家公司。美国限制哪些芯片？由于先进人工智能具有军事应用，华盛顿以安全考虑为由，禁止英伟达高端“Blackwell”和“Rubin”GPU出口到中国。该政策还让美国顶级人工智能实验室保持全球领先地位。
黄仁勋游说美国政府允许 Nvidia 芯片销售到中国，并警告说这些限制正在推动具有竞争力的本土替代品的崛起。Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2025 年 5 月 19 日在台湾台北举行的 Computex 2025 上发表主题演讲。照片：Nvidia。今年，华盛顿放松了对 Nvidia 之前被禁止且功能较弱的“H200”芯片的控制，美国的销售额减少了 25%。但美国的条件使得发货很难获得批准，据报道，随着中国自己的芯片行业发展势头强劲，北京方面也不愿购买 H200。中国如何获得芯片？中国初创公司最近推出的高性能模型，包括 Moonshot AI、Z.ai 和 DeepSeek，给美国竞争对手带来了压力。 Omdia 首席分析师 Lian Jye Su 告诉法新社，尽管有控制措施，“中国供应商仍在使用先进的 Nvidia 芯片来训练他们的模型”。芯片可能被走私到该国，或者通过一个漏洞获得，该漏洞允许中国公司在第三国（通常是东南亚）的装有英伟达芯片的数据中心出租计算能力。深探。照片：Matheus Bertelli/Pexels。迦太基资本投资基金创始人斯蒂芬·吴解释说：“美国的出口管制限制了芯片的运输地点，而不是使用它的人。”吴告诉法新社，这意味着 Nvidia GPU 可以安装在马来西亚的柔佛地区，“在深圳的客户登录时完全符合要求”。
白宫顾问 Michael Kratsios 今年夏天表示，Moonshot AI 已在泰国访问了 Nvidia 的高端芯片。另请参阅：被指控监视 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋的中国科技高管 Alice Huang 是谁？华盛顿还指责中国人工智能实验室的训练系统模仿美国模型的能力。还有一个大问题是走私。科技媒体 The Information 去年 12 月表示，DeepSeek 使用数千块在海外拆解并运回中国的芯片开发了其新模型。 DeepSeek 当时没有回应评论请求。英伟达告诉 The Information，他们还没有看到此类走私的证据，这“似乎有些遥远”

【原文 English Original】
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, reportedly with a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based company that the United States suspects of smuggling AI microchips into China. Nvidia’s H200 chips. Photo: Nvidia. The scandal has focused attention on how China, a major artificial-intelligence power in itself, obtains the cutting-edge chips despite US export restrictions. Why are Nvidia chips so important? Nvidia designs advanced components originally created to handle 3D visuals in video games, called Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). These have the power to crunch colossal amounts of digital data, so are also used at scale to train and run artificial intelligence. ChatGPT’s 2022 launch showcased the potential of AI, sparking an investment gold rush as governments and tech giants raced to develop the technology further. Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California. Photo: Nvidia. With chip orders pouring in, Nvidia’s market valuation has soared to $4.5 trillion — currently on par with Apple as the world’s two most valuable companies. Which chips does the US restrict? Washington bans the export of Nvidia’s top-end “Blackwell” and “Rubin” GPUs to China, citing security concerns, as advanced AI has military applications. The policy also allows the United States’s top AI labs to maintain their global lead. Huang has lobbied the US government to allow Nvidia chip sales to China, warning that the restrictions are fuelling the rise of competitive homegrown alternatives. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang gives a keynote speech at Computex 2025 in Taipei, Taiwan, on May 19, 2025. Photo: Nvidia. This year Washington eased controls on Nvidia’s previously banned — and less powerful — “H200” chip, with the United States taking a 25 percent cut of sales. But US conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also reportedly reluctant to buy H200s as its own chip industry gains momentum. How does China get its chips? Recent launches of high-performing models from Chinese startups, including Moonshot AI, Z.ai and DeepSeek, have turned up the heat on US rivals. “Chinese vendors are still using cutting-edge Nvidia chips to train their models” despite the controls, Lian Jye Su, a chief analyst at Omdia, told AFP. Chips may be smuggled into the country, or accessed through a loophole that allows Chinese firms to rent out computing power at data centres stuffed with Nvidia chips in a third nation, often Southeast Asian. Deepseek. Photo: Matheus Bertelli/Pexels. “US export controls restrict where a chip is shipped, not who uses it,” explained Stephen Wu, founder of the Carthage Capital investment fund. That means Nvidia GPUs can sit in Malaysia’s Johor region, for example, “in full compliance while a customer in Shenzhen logs in”, Wu told AFP. White House adviser Michael Kratsios said this summer that Moonshot AI had accessed high-end Nvidia chips in Thailand. See also: Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese tech executive accused of spying on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang? Washington has also accused Chinese AI labs of training systems to mimic the capabilities of US models. And then there is the big question of smuggling. Tech outlet The Information said in December that DeepSeek developed its new model using thousands of chips dismantled overseas and brought into China. DeepSeek did not respond to a comment request at the time. Nvidia told The Information they had not seen evidence of such smuggling which “seems far-fetched”. How about Chinese chips? “Nvidia chips still make top-level AI work faster and easier, but they are no longer the only path,” said Poe Zhao, founder of analysis publication Hello China Tech. “The open question is cost” as “training on Chinese chips usually takes more time and more engineering”. Huawei is China’s top Nvidia competitor, although it lags behind the US titan, and DeepSeek will reportedly train its next major AI model on Huawei chips. Huawei headquarters in Shenzhen. Photo: Huawei. “Chinese-made chips are improving fast”, Su said, with more collaborations likely to come. Huawei said in September its next-generation AI chip would be ready in the first quarter of 2027, three quarters earlier than planned. To boost the power of Chinese-made chips, AI companies need to use more of them, Wu said. “They pay for it in power and cost — which they can afford, because Chinese electricity is cheap and the chips are state-subsidised.”

content:
《神爱世人系列》第二篇：神为什么爱世人 – 罗兰岗召会 Church In Rowland Heights
亲爱的弟兄姊妹，第一篇我们看见：神爱世人，因为神就是爱。这一篇要再问深一层：神为什么偏偏这样爱人？万物之中，神造了天地万有，为什么祂的爱单单这样倾注在人身上？答案藏在创造里：人不是偶然的，乃是神亲手设计、亲手塑造的器皿，为着盛装祂自己。神爱人，因为人在祂永远的计划里有无可替代的地位。
创世记一章二十六至二十七节说：“神说，我们要按着我们的形像，照着我们的样式造人，使他们管理海里的鱼、空中的鸟、地上的牲畜、和全地、并地上所爬的一切爬物。神就按着自己的形像创造人，乃是按着神的形像创造他；创造他们有男有女。”
万物都是神「说有就有」，惟有人，是三一神开会商议之后造的：「我们要……造人。」形像是里面的所像——人的心思、情感、意志，像神一样能思想、能爱、能拣选；样式是外面的形状。人被造得像神，因为人要在地上代表神、彰显神。神爱人，第一，因为人是宇宙中惟一按祂形像造的——人是祂的「亲像」，祂看着人，就像看着自己的照片，祂不能不爱。
创世记二章七节说：“耶和华神用地上的尘土塑造人，将生命之气吹在他鼻孔里，人就成了活的魂。”
请注意两个动作：神「塑造」人——像陶匠亲手捏塑，用的是祂自己的手；神又把生命之气「吹」在人鼻孔里——用的是祂自己的口。万物没有一样得着这样的待遇。人是神手里的作品，又带着神口中的气息。人里面最高贵的部分，就是为着盛装神的：身体是尘土作的，魂是人活着的自己，而人的深处还有灵，是为着接触神、盛装神的。神爱人，因为人是祂亲手作的，带着祂的亲手和亲气。
罗马书九章二十一节说：“窑匠难道没有权柄，从同一团泥里，拿一块作成贵重的器皿，又拿一块作成卑贱的器皿么？”保罗把神比作窑匠，把人比作祂手中的器皿。器皿的意义，不在器皿自己，乃在它所盛装的。一个杯子再精美，若永远是空的，就失去了它被造的目的；人也是这样：人被造，是一个有容量、有空间的器皿，为着装一样东西——就是神自己。
罗马书九章二十三节接着说：“且要在那些蒙怜悯、早豫备得荣耀的器皿上，彰显祂荣耀的丰富；”我们这些器皿，是「蒙怜悯」的，是神「早豫备得荣耀的」。神预备我们，不是为着摆设，乃是要在我们身上彰显祂荣耀的丰富。神爱世人，因为世人是祂豫备好要装满祂荣耀的器皿——祂舍不得让这器皿空着，更舍不得让它被别的东西霸占。
哥林多后书四章七节说：“但我们有这宝贝在瓦器里，要显明这超越的能力，是属于神，不是出于我们；”瓦器是廉价、脆弱的，宝贝却是无价的。保罗说，我们这瓦器里有「这宝贝」——就是基督，就是神自己。外面的器皿不值什么，里面的内容无价；这衬托出神爱的智慧：祂不嫌弃我们是瓦器，反倒把祂最宝贵的自己，放进我们这瓦器里面。祂爱我们，爱到把自己给了我们，住在我们里面。
歌罗西书一章二十七节说：“神愿意叫他们知道，这奥秘的荣耀在外邦人中是何等的丰富，就是基督在你们里面成了荣耀的盼望。”这就是器皿被造的答案：基督在我们里面。神爱世人，不只是怜悯世人，更是要进到人里面，与人调和，让人盛装祂、彰显祂，直到人被祂的荣耀浸透，成为祂荣耀的彰显。这就是下一篇我们要看的：这位爱人的神，如何把祂的爱实际地显明出来——差祂的独生子，降生到世人中间。
• 看见真理：神爱世人，因为人是祂按形像造、亲手塑造、豫备得荣耀的器皿，为着盛装基督。
• 享受真理：不要轻看自己——你不是没人要的瓦片，你是神手里豫备好装宝贝的器皿；每天向主敞开：「主阿，我是你的器皿，求你今天多装一点进来。」
• 活出真理：器皿的功用是装、是给——让基督从我们里面流出去，给家人、给同事、给福音朋友，叫他们也看见这器皿里的宝贝。
主耶稣，我们敬拜你。你是窑匠，我们是泥土；你按着你的形像造我们，用你的手塑造我们，用你的气吹进我们里面。主阿，我们不配，你却把你自己这无价的宝贝，放在我们这瓦器里。我们把自己再一次向你敞开：主，充满我们，浸透我们，叫基督在我们里面，真正成为荣耀的盼望。奉主耶稣的名祷告，阿们，哈利路亚！
我虽然行过死荫的幽谷，也不怕遭害，因为你与我同在；你的杖，你的竿，都安慰我。
在我敌人面前，你为我摆设筵席；你用油膏了我的头，使我的福杯满溢。
我一生一世必有恩惠慈爱随着我，我且要住在耶和华的殿中，直到永远。

title: Pixel Tag, Google’s $30 Android-ready answer to Apple’s AirTag, is now available
summary: Pixel Tag, Google's $30 Android-ready answer to Apple's AirTag, is now available | TechCrunch Pixel Tag, Google’s $30 Android-ready answer to Apple’s AirTag, is now available 10:49 AM PST · November 10, 2026 Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTa
content:
Pixel Tag, Google's $30 Android-ready answer to Apple's AirTag, is now available | TechCrunch
Pixel Tag, Google’s $30 Android-ready answer to Apple’s AirTag, is now available
10:49 AM PST · November 10, 2026
Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTag, the Google Pixel Tag, goes on sale starting Tuesday, allowing Android users to track items like their keys, wallet, or bag using their smartphone’s built-in Find Hub.
First announced in August, the $29.99 device takes cues from the AirTag and other lost-item finders by offering connectivity via Bluetooth and ultra-wideband for precision finding. This lets Android device owners, including Pixel Watch wearers, locate their missing items using a combination of visual distance and directional guidance.
Plus, the tag has a built-in speaker to play a chime that helps you locate your item if nearby. (Or, if you’ve lost your phone, you can press the button on the Pixel Tag twice to ring it, too.) You can choose between three different levels of loudness in the settings within the Find Hub, with the maximum volume around 80 decibels.
Though the Pixel Tag serves the same purpose as an AirTag, Google has opted for a different design. Instead of a small, round device, like Apple’s, the Pixel Tag is slimmer and more elongated.
Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1-inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8-inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height). The slimness of the device might make it more appealing for some, particularly if they’re adding the tag to a small item, like a keychain.
The device weighs just 0.4 oz, with the battery included.
Unlike Apple, Google opted for a physical button you can press on the tag, which makes it more obvious how it’s meant to work.
Google didn’t originally say that the Pixel Tag included NFC when it announced the device in August. NFC is used by Apple’s AirTag to aid people who find lost items, as they can tap the side of the tag to launch a webpage that displays the owner’s contact information. Google uses the tap gesture to instead connect the user to the device’s settings.
Meanwhile, for lost items that are not nearby, the Pixel Tag relies on Google’s crowdsourced network of over a billion Android devices globally. The network, similar to competitive offerings from Apple and Tile, taps into the connectivity provided by other Android devices, which can identify and share the location of the lost item back to its owner. This location information is displayed on a map inside the Find Hub app.
While the person who found the item can’t tap it, as with NFC-enabled devices, Pixel Tags that are put into “Lost” mode will be able to share the owner’s email, number, and a short message so the person who finds the tag can contact you. When the tag comes back into range of the user’s phone, the item is automatically marked as found.
The Pixel Tag’s location can also be shared with up to 10 people in the Find Hub app, which could be useful for shared items like the family car keys, which multiple people might rely on.
Like AirTag, the Pixel Tag is powered by a user-replaceable coin cell battery (the CR2032), which makes the device reusable for the long term. (Google claims the device has up to one year of battery life to start.)
Meanwhile, the device itself is made from stainless steel and features IP67 water and dust resistance (maximum depth of 1 meter up to 30 minutes). It pairs with devices running Android 9 or newer via Fast Pair technology.
The Pixel Tag comes in two shades: silver and a pale green, and can be bought individually or in a four-pack for $99.99.
Alongside the launch, the company Bellroy is debuting its own keychain cases in a variety of colors and styles, which will also be sold on the Google Store.
Post updated after publication to note that the Pixel Tag now supports NFC, which was a surprise addition not mentioned at the time of its announcement.

title: 英伟达股价再次下滑，CEO黄仁勋面临诉讼及FBI调查

content: 在华盛顿美国和平研究所举行的一场活动中，英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统发言时倾听。(2026年10月8日) 英伟达(Nvidia)股价星期二(11月10日)连续第二天走低，这家位于美国的半导体公司首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)同时面临股东诉讼，并承受着来自国会日益增长的压力。 此次抛售的前一天，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)说，联邦调查局(FBI)正在调查黄仁勋与女商人黄乐(Alice Huang)之间的关系；美国情报部门认定，这名女商人是在为中国搜集情报。 英伟达董事会于星期日启动了独立审查，原因是有报道指黄仁勋成为外国情报机构的目标。黄仁勋在发给员工的一则信息中承认自己曾有不忠行为，但未透露女方身份。 特朗普与黄仁勋通话 英伟达股价在星期二上午交易时段下跌了5.3%。星期一收盘时，该股下跌了4.3%，导致公司市值缩水约1900亿美元。 特朗普在星期一的白宫简报会上说，他曾致电黄仁勋，询问其近况。 特朗普说，“我问了他那个问题：‘你知不知道她是间谍？’他说‘我完全不知道她是间谍。’我确实相信他，”“我知道联邦调查局正在调查此事，”“我认为他会没事的。” 特朗普将于下星期前往中国深圳参加亚太经合组织峰会，届时他预计将与中国国家主席习近平会晤。当被问及是否会向习提及此事时，特朗普说，“不，我想不会。我是说，也许吧。我相信习近平主席会问起这件事的。” 中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期二在北京拒绝表明习近平是否会提出这一问题。他仅表示，双方正在就两国领导人今年的会晤安排进行讨论。中方已否认了有关间谍指控。 投资人诉讼 散户投资者马克·基斯滕马赫(Mark Kistenmacher)星期一在加利福尼亚州圣何塞的联邦法院对英伟达及黄仁勋提起诉讼；他在一份拟议的集体诉讼中指控他们欺骗了股东。根据起诉书，英伟达隐瞒了相关事宜，并对其与Megaspeed公司之间的往来情况进行了失实陈述；Megaspeed是一家位于新加坡的企业，黄乐曾在此担任高管。诉讼文件指称，此举使英伟达的声誉和业务面临“重大风险”。 原告要求由陪审团审理此案，并寻求损害赔偿，但未明确具体金额。诉讼涵盖10月9日至11月8日期间买入英伟达股票的股东。英伟达未立即就此诉讼置评。 议员们要求给出答复 众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯(Hakeem Jeffries)星期一说，“显然，国会需要更多信息。”杰弗里斯说。当天在中央情报局局长约翰·拉特克利夫(John Ratcliffe)和国家情报总监杰伊·克莱顿(Jay Clayton)参加的机密简报会上，伊朗问题占据了主导地位，英伟达只是被顺带提及。 马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦(Elizabeth Warren)和印第安纳州共和党参议员吉姆·班克斯(Jim Banks)星期一在一份联合声明中说，这一事件使国家安全方面的担忧“变得更加紧迫”。他们敦促国会将《人工智能监管法案》(AI Overwatch Act)这个让国会能够监督最先进芯片出口的法案，纳入年度国防法案。 来自特拉瓦州的民主党参议员克里斯·库恩斯(Chris Coons)在X上写道，他正在“推动对黄仁勋及英伟达展开调查，以确定我们的国家安全是否受到了损害。”

而在伊朗的局势方面，特朗普总统星期一在白宫会见卡塔尔首相阿勒萨尼之后在白宫表示，美军对伊朗持续严阵以待，但目前“没有必要发动进一步的军事行动”。美国国务卿卢比奥星期二也在巴黎举行的七国集团外长会上表示，美国对伊朗实施的经济制裁和海上封锁效果显著，已使特朗普总统没有必要再对伊朗发动大规模的军事行动。此外，卢比奥国务卿也在G7结束后，特别谈到了美中之间的大国竞争，他强调，美中双方都将本国的利益置于首位。来看美国之音的电视报道。
卢比奥国务卿在巴黎与七国集团的盟友举行了为期两天的会谈后向记者表示，美国暂时搁置军事行动并不代表陷入僵局。卢比奥国务卿说：“我们的经济行动，以及由此对伊朗政权施加的压力和造成的经济破坏，效果非常显著，以至于总统实际上已经没有必要再发动大规模军事行动。当然，如果伊朗触碰某些红线，或者伊朗政权采取某些不应该发生的行动，我不会具体推测这些情况是什么，但你们知道我指的是什么，美国军方作为世界上最具作战能力的军队，随时准备采取行动应对。”
卢比奥国务卿强调，在美军暂停打击的同时，美国对伊朗的经济制裁仍将持续加强，随着伊朗仅存的石油库存耗尽，美国财政部长贝森特也正在与情报机构合作，致力防堵伊朗规避制裁的漏洞。
而谈到美中之间的大国竞争，卢比奥国务卿重申，他对美中之间在各个议题上的分歧与中国的体制，始终保持务实而清醒的态度：“我们并非为全球秩序服务，也不是为其他国家效力；我们是为美国服务。在处理各类政策议题时，无论是涉及我们与其他国家的双边关系，还是人工智能的发展，我们始终将美国及其人民的利益置于一切之上。这往往使我们与包括中国在内的其他国家产生分歧或冲突。我们对此保持务实而清醒的态度。我是在为美国工作，总统也在为美国而战。在任何议题上，我们永远都会站在美国这一边。”
至于有媒体报道，卢比奥国务卿对英伟达CEO黄仁勋的婚外情可能涉及中共间谍与美中科技竞争，事先知情，并监督起草一份备忘录向特朗普政府高层发出警告，在巴黎面对记者追问此事时，卢比奥国务卿回应称，无法对相关报道发表评论。

title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
summary: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google | TechCrunch OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google 10:49 AM PST · November 10, 2026 In an effort t
content:
OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google | TechCrunch
OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
10:49 AM PST · November 10, 2026
In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses.
On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta.
Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products.
“As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.”
In a move that calls to mind Google Analytics, the Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights. These insights will reveal how ChatGPT users interact with their products — including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics.
Businesses will have to verify their profiles through a formal process, although the company did not share specifics of what that process would entail. Benji Shomair, OpenAI’s VP of Monetization, told journalists on Monday that there are “multiple verification methods that we use for different types of business in different markets.”
OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort, which had even included a “checkout cart” feature.
With the integration of business profiles and intelligence, ChatGPT seems to be attempting to become more like Google, which — since the advent of the internet — has been the place where web users go to understand the companies they want to shop at. It remains to be seen whether this initiative will bear better results than the one that sought to make ChatGPT a direct e-commerce hub.

content: 追光者  2026-11-10 【輝達黃仁勳剛認婚外情 特朗普再爆某AI大公司負責人利用AI做壞事：準備坐牢吧】 輝達創辦人黃仁勳周日（8日）承認婚外情震撼全球，情婦背景愈挖愈多，更有傳她是有夫之婦，丈夫因違法被捕。同時，美國總統特朗普透露，某AI大公司負責人「利用AI做壞事」，更致電通知對方「準備坐牢吧」。不過，他拒絕公開對方身份。 黃仁勳出軌掀起巨浪，輝達周一（9日）股價重挫4.27%，收報178.67美元，單日市值蒸發1,900億美元。有股東在收市後隨即向加州聖荷西聯邦法院入稟，就輝達蓄意隱瞞黃仁勳與疑似中國女間諜的親密關係、嚴重誤導並欺騙股東，造成公司重大全球商譽和營運風險，涉違反證券交易相關法規，向輝達和黃仁勳發起集體訴訟。 ︱前央視記者證曾共事 傳為有夫之婦 股東興訟之際，情婦黃樂的身世之謎繼續被起底，對於其4年媒體經驗曾任職中國湖南衛視和央視的說法，有前央視記者在微博發文，稱曾與黃樂在同一間辦公室共事，並形容當年就覺得對方「不簡單」。 中國《財新網》則引述知情人士報道，現年約42歲的黃樂，曾在約20年前在香港浸會大學傳理學院攻讀媒體管理碩士課程。 更為人好奇的是黃樂的婚姻狀況，中國媒體眾說紛云，有知情人士指她的丈夫是於上海和熙投資擔任合夥人時的拍檔康偉，惟康偉因違反證券法遭判刑；對於康偉的傳言亦有不同版本，有指他涉及走私輝達晶片，另一說法則指他涉及非法集資上百億，被中共查抄判無期徒刑；甚至有流傳康偉「獻祭」黃樂予黃仁勳來維持新加坡公司Megaspeed與輝達的合作關係。 ︱特朗普致電黃仁勳 黃稱完全不知道她是間諜 對於黃樂的身份，不止民眾，連特朗普也好奇。特朗普昨於白宮記者會回應聯邦調查局（FBI）會調查事件，又指即日已致電黃仁勳，詢問他知否女方是間諜，黃稱「我完全不知道她是間諜」，特朗普直認相信黃仁勳，又認為黃正承受着巨大的痛苦。 對於下周到深圳出席APEC峰會將與中國國家主席習近平會晤，特朗普被問到會否向習近平提起疑似中國間諜一事時，他稱不打算提出，但他認為習會問及此事，重申認為黃仁勳是非常可敬之人。特朗普早前曾表態，願意帶黃仁勳同行前往中國。 ︱特朗普爆某AI大公司負責人做壞事 未透露詳情 力撐黃仁勳的同時，特朗普在哥倫比亞廣播公司（CBS）節目「60分鐘」（60 Minutes）周日播出的專訪爆料，司法部曾接獲通報，指有人「利用AI做壞事」，隔天早上可能會將他逮捕，因此「我們以非常強硬的態度打電話給對方警告：準備坐牢吧，請親吻你的妻子，向她說晚安」。 不過，特朗普這番說話到底是在威脅誰，他沒有鬆口，僅確認是一家大型AI公司的負責人。他又指，對方隨後「徹底改變作法」，卻未明言後續的調查情況或有否採取執法行動。

title: Update Chrome now to fix a flaw attackers are exploiting
zh_title: 立即更新 Chrome 以修复攻击者利用的漏洞
summary: 11 月 9 日，谷歌发布了适用于 Windows、Mac 和 Linux 的 Chrome 稳定频道的安全更新。该更新将在未来几天和几周内推出。大多数用户都使用 Chrome 的稳定渠道。此次桌面更新将 Chrome 带到了 Windows 和 Mac 版本 157.0.8103.50/.51 以及 Linux 版本 157.0.8103.50。它包括九个安全修复程序，其中一个针对被积极利用的零日漏洞。零日漏洞是在官方修复可用之前披露或利用的安全缺陷。香港计算机紧急应变小组协调中心（HKCERT）
content:
11 月 9 日，谷歌发布了适用于 Windows、Mac 和 Linux 的 Chrome 稳定频道的安全更新。该更新将在未来几天和几周内推出。大多数用户都使用 Chrome 的稳定渠道。此次桌面更新将 Chrome 带到了 Windows 和 Mac 版本 157.0.8103.50/.51 以及 Linux 版本 157.0.8103.50。它包括九个安全修复程序，其中一个针对被积极利用的零日漏洞。零日漏洞是在官方修复可用之前披露或利用的安全缺陷。香港计算机应急响应小组协调中心（HKCERT）将总体风险评级为“极高”。其公告称，更新中解决的一些漏洞可能允许拒绝服务、安全限制绕过和远程代码执行。如何更新 Chrome 最简单的选择是允许 Chrome 自动更新。但是，如果您从未关闭浏览器或出现问题（例如扩展程序阻止更新），您最终可能会落后于更新。如果您不想等待发布，您可以手动更新。从 Chrome 的“设置”或“帮助”菜单中打开“关于 Google Chrome”。 Chrome 将检查更新并下载任何可用的更新。如果出现提示，请单击“重新启动”以应用它。 Chrome 157.0.8103.51 已更新 您可以在我们的指南中找到版本编号系统的说明和分步说明：如何在每个操作系统上更新 Chrome 。
谷歌还于 11 月 9 日发布了 Android 版 Chrome 157.0.8103.50。谷歌表示，除非另有说明，否则它包含与桌面版本相同的安全修复程序。 Android 用户应检查 Google Play 是否有更新。技术细节让我们仔细看看这个零日漏洞。谷歌表示，它于 11 月 6 日收到未具名第三方的漏洞通知。该漏洞被追踪为 CVE-2026-125350，并被评为 Chrome XML 组件中的高严重性释放后使用漏洞。 XML 是 Chrome 用来读取和处理某些类型的结构化 Web 内容的数据格式。 XML 代表可扩展标记语言：它使用标签来标记信息，就像 HTML 一样，但允许作者定义自己的标签来描述他们的数据。当程序尝试访问已释放的内存位置时，就会发生释放后使用漏洞。这可能会导致崩溃，或者在某些情况下，允许攻击者运行自己的代码。谷歌仅表示“意识到 CVE-2026-125350 的漏洞存在”。它没有透露攻击者、目标、交付方法或该漏洞可以做什么。在威胁造成任何伤害之前阻止它们。 Malwarebytes Browser Guard 自动阻止网络钓鱼页面和恶意网站。免费，一键安装。将其添加到您的浏览器 →

【原文 English Original】
On November 9, Google issued a security update to Chrome’s Stable channel for Windows, Mac, and Linux. The update is rolling out over the coming days and weeks. Most users are on Chrome’s Stable channel. The desktop update brings Chrome to versions 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux . It includes nine security fixes, including one for an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability. A zero-day vulnerability is a security flaw disclosed or exploited before an official fix becomes available. Hong Kong’s Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) rates the overall risk as “Extremely High.” Its bulletin says some of the vulnerabilities address in the update could allow denial of service, security restriction bypass, and remote code execution. How to update Chrome The easiest option is to allow Chrome to update automatically. But you can end up lagging behind on updates if you never close your browser or if something goes wrong, such as an extension preventing the update. If you don’t want to wait for the rollout to reach you, you can update manually. Open About Google Chrome from Chrome’s Settings or Help menu. Chrome will check for updates and download any available update. If prompted, click Relaunch to apply it. Chrome 157.0.8103.51 is up to date You can find an explanation of the version numbering system and step-by-step instructions in our guide: How to update Chrome on every operating system . Google also released Chrome 157.0.8103.50 for Android on November 9. Google says it includes the same security fixes as the desktop release unless otherwise noted. Android users should check Google Play for the update. Technical details Let’s take a closer look at that zero-day vulnerability. Google says it was notified about a vulnerability by an unnamed third party on November 6. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-125350 and rated as a high-severity use-after-free vulnerability in Chrome’s XML component. XML is a data format Chrome uses to read and process certain kinds of structured web content. XML stands for Extensible Markup Language: it labels information with tags, rather like HTML, but allows authors to define their own tags to describe their data. A use-after-free vulnerability occurs when a program attempts to access a memory location after it has been freed. That can cause crashes or, in some cases, allow an attacker to run their own code. Google only says that it is “aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild.” It has not named the attackers, the targets, the delivery method, or what the exploit can do. title: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
summary: All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO | TechCrunch Image Credits:Evan-Marie Petit Photography All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO 11:57 AM PST · November 10, 2026 As Anthropic barrels towa
content:
All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO | TechCrunch
Image Credits:Evan-Marie Petit Photography
All 7 Anthropic founders will each cash out about $250M in IPO
11:57 AM PST · November 10, 2026
As Anthropic barrels toward an enormous IPO that could value it at $1.4 trillion, the company has disclosed a tidbit in its new S-1 filing about how many shares each of its seven co-founders plan to sell.
Each will sell 3,378,378 shares. Anthropic has floated an unusually broad initial price range of $70 to $78 a share. At the midrange of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million.
At the low end, $70, each would have to settle for pocketing just over $236 million in cash; at the high end, $78, each would take in just under $264 million.
However, in an IPO as eagerly anticipated as this one, companies can often price shares above the initial range.
The S-1 is already hinting at high demand. Board member Reed Hastings has indicated he wants to buy $300 million worth of shares through his donor-advised fund. Board member Christopher Liddell also wants to buy $3 million worth of shares.
The seven co-founders are Dario Amodei, CEO; Daniela Amodei, president and chair of the board; Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of public benefit; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer (pictured above); Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, interpretability research lead.
After the sale, each of them will own about 3.2% of the total outstanding Class A shares, the S-1 says, or roughly 22% collectively. That’s not their share of the company overall. Class A is just one of Anthropic’s share classes, and other holders, including Amazon and Google, hold nonvoting Class N shares, so the founders’ stake in the company’s total equity will be considerably smaller. Even still, they, as a group, remain in control of the company. Each will also receive one share of Class F stock, which carries supervoting rights. Collectively, the founders will control 51.1% of the votes, but no single founder will hold significantly more shares or votes than the others.
As is now industry lore, the seven left OpenAI to start Anthropic in 2021 after disagreements with OpenAI’s leadership over how AI should be built. Siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, who held senior research and policy roles at OpenAI, were joined by five fellow OpenAI colleagues in forming a company that has said, very publicly and from the start, that it’s more focused on AI safety than its rivals, including the founders’ former employer.

content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

title: Microsoft lobbies against potential ban on Chinese optical networking gear for AI data centers as FCC mulls restricting imports
zh_title: FCC 考虑限制进口，微软游说反对针对人工智能数据中心的中国光网络设备的潜在禁令
summary: 据报道，科技巨头微软正在美国各地建设 35 个数据中心，并计划再建设 134 个数据中心，据报道，微软已与白宫科学技术政策办公室和国家安全委员会会面，因为 FCC 正在考虑禁止进口中国光收发器。据路透社报道，该公司与信息技术产业委员会（ITI）一起游说反对此举。深入了解 TH Premium：人工智能和数据中心（图片来源：微软） 数据中心冷却现状 定制 AI ASIC 现状 美国的人工智能芯片规则不断变化
content:
据报道，科技巨头微软正在美国各地建设 35 个数据中心，并计划再建设 134 个数据中心，据报道，微软已与白宫科学技术政策办公室和国家安全委员会会面，因为 FCC 正在考虑禁止进口中国光收发器。据路透社报道，该公司与信息技术产业委员会（ITI）一起游说反对此举。深入了解 TH Premium：AI 和数据中心（图片来源：Microsoft） 数据中心冷却现状 定制 AI ASIC 现状 美国的 AI 芯片规则不断变化，而世界其他国家正在为此付出代价 GTC 2026：Ian Buck 新闻问答记录 — 超大规模和 HPC 副总裁就今年搁置 CPX 和运输 LPU 解码发表讲话 对数据中心 CPU 的需求激增，AI 代理对此负责“这确实威胁到了磨合” （数据中心的推出）暂停，”ITI 政策执行副总裁兼总法律顾问 John Miller 表示。他还补充道，“这些没有光学收发器的芯片实际上可能只是坐在那里等待未使用，直到你真正拥有收发器将它们基本上连接在一起”，他指的是数据中心使用的人工智能芯片。光收发器是插入硬件中的微型模块，可将电信号转换为光信号，从而允许数据以光脉冲的形式通过光纤传输。
数据中心越来越多地使用光收发器和光纤在 AI GPU 和服务器机架之间传输数据，因为与传统的铜连接相比，它们速度更快、延迟更低、功耗更低、产生的热量更少。然而，中国公司目前供应全球 66% 的市场，这意味着禁止他们向美国数据中心供货将使可用供应量减少一半以上，从而加剧一直困扰该行业的各种短缺问题。然而，有人担心其中一些收发器可能会被北京破坏，并被用来窃取数据、安装恶意软件或远程破坏美国数据中心，这就是 FCC 正在考虑实施限制的原因，就像它禁止华为进入美国电信网络一样。但与在电信硬件行业拥有众多老牌竞争对手的华为不同，只有两家美国公司生产数据中心所需的光收发器——相干公司和 Lumentum。虽然这些公司可以生产光收发器来与中国产品竞争，但如果联邦通信委员会今天禁止从中国进口，它们根本没有规模来弥补缺口。特朗普政府提出的一项妥协方案是，仅禁止能够达到每秒 3.2 兆比特的中国光收发器。虽然这项技术已经存在，但预计其生产要到 2028 年才会扩大，安装要到 2029 年才会开始。
这应该会让美国生产商有时间增加自己的产量，尽管该建议仍在考虑中。

【原文 English Original】
Microsoft, the tech giant that is building 35 data centers around the U.S. and has plans for 134 more, has reportedly met with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Security Council as the FCC is considering an import ban on Chinese optical transceivers . According to Reuters , the company, alongside the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI), is lobbying against the move. Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft) The data center cooling state of play The custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible “It really threatens to arguably grind (the data center rollout) to a halt,” ITI Executive Vice President of Policy and General Counsel John Miller said. He also added, “Those chips, without optical transceivers, literally could just sit there waiting around unutilized until you actually have the transceivers to essentially connect them together,” referring to the AI chips that data centers use. Optical transceivers are tiny modules plugged into hardware that convert their electrical signals into light signals, allowing data to be transmitted as light pulses across fiber optics. Data centers increasingly use optical transceivers and fiber optics to transmit data between AI GPUs and server racks, as they’re faster, offer lower latency, require less power, and generate less heat compared to traditional copper connections. However, Chinese companies currently supply 66% of the global market, meaning banning them from supplying data centers in the U.S. would more than halve the available supply, thereby exacerbating the various shortages that have been pummeling the industry . However, there are concerns that some of these transceivers could be compromised by Beijing and be used to steal data, install malware, or remotely disrupt American data centers, which is why the FCC is considering the restriction, just like how it banned Huawei from the U.S. telecommunications network. But unlike Huawei, which had many established competitors in the telecommunications hardware industry, only two U.S.-based companies produce optical transceivers that data centers need — Coherent and Lumentum. While these firms could produce optical transceivers to compete with Chinese offerings, they simply do not have the scale to make up for the shortfall if the FCC bans Chinese imports today. One compromise floated by the Trump administration is that it would only ban Chinese optical transceivers capable of hitting 3.2 terabits per second. While this technology already exists, its production isn’t expected to expand until 2028, with installation not beginning until 2029. This should give American producers time to ramp up their own output, although the suggestion is still under consideration.
